issues.failure_explanation: The displayed memory balance is not a bound on a nonnegative energy. Choose ν₁=a<ν₂=b, φ¹=w and φ²=0. For sufficiently small τ, b₂₂>b₁₁ and E₂=½[b₁₁−(2−2^(1−b))b₂₂]||w||²<0, since b₁₁/b₂₂ tends to zero. Continuous admissible order profiles can have these two values. Scaling w makes the functional arbitrarily negative; for a fixed spatial mode this negative contribution can also dominate the O(τ) dissipation term. No lower bound or estimate controlling R is supplied. Thus the algebraic inequality does not establish the advertised stability.

Ordinary approximation properties of the full velocity space do not imply approximation in its discretely divergence-free subspace. For example, continuous P₁ velocities and elementwise P₀ pressures are allowed. issues.failure_explanation: The defined velocity projector depends on the pair (u,p), not on u alone. Take u=0, B=0 and a nonconstant pressure, with f=∇p. issues.failure_explanation: The mesh is only called a triangulation; no shape-regularity or quasi-uniformity condition is stated. On a locally refined mesh with a patch of diameter ε much smaller than the global mesh size h, a nodal function supported on that patch has ||∇v_h||/||v_h|| of order ε⁻¹ and ||v_h||₄/||v_h|| of order ε⁻¹ᐟ². Thus the asserted global-h inverse estimates need not have a uniform constant. Their use does not justify the claimed h-independent nonlinear-error coefficient on the stated mesh class.

issues.failure_explanation: Only a bounded first time derivative is assumed. For constant order a and φ(t)=t^(1+σ), with 0<σ<a, that regularity holds, but at the first step the L1 residual is [Γ(2+σ)/Γ(2+σ−a)−1/Γ(2−a)]τ^(1+σ−a). Its nonzero coefficient and exponent below one show that it is not O(τ). Multiplying this example by a smooth divergence-free spatial field gives the same obstruction within the solution regularity class. The replacement of the squared residuals by Cτ² in the convergence proof is therefore unsupported.

issues.failure_explanation: With δ fixed, the uniform limit as ε tends to zero is the constant order 1−δ, not 1. In fact, the sup-norm distance from order one is ε+δ and tends to δ. The stated one-parameter test therefore does not realize the classical limit it is claimed to verify; it supplies finite-offset near-classical comparisons.
